1. standards/standards/options-ui.md: append after §20 (the last section; file ends at line 498) `### 21. Label and tooltip conventions (v2.88.0)`. Intro paragraph: 'A player who has read one Ka0s settings page reads the next without relearning its words. These rules fix the words; options-ui-§7, §13, §14, §15 and §16 fix where rows go. They bind every row label, tab label, subsection and grid heading, rail entry, column header, button text, tooltip and location string the settings draw, and the chat route lines and drag-handle tooltips that name a settings location. Composed rows keep the composer's words (§15, §16): nothing here licenses a host to rewrite them.' Then these bullets (smooth the prose, keep every quoted string and every MUST/SHOULD exactly):
   - **Case (MUST).** Sentence case for row labels, tab labels, subsection and grid headings, rail entries, column headers and button text. Title Case only for sidebar page names (the client's list title-cases them), proper nouns, and entity names shown as list entries (a message name, a statistic name).
   - **Two subjects (MUST).** Join with 'and', never '&' (*Size and position*, *Background and border*).
   - **Units (MUST).** Pixels '(px)'. Time '(seconds)', or '(seconds left)' where it reads better. Otherwise '(%)', '(degrees)', '(characters)', '(item levels)'. A sentinel shares the parenthesis: '(px, 0 = automatic)', '(seconds, 0 = no limit)'. Never '(in px)', '(in seconds)', '(sec)' or '(s)'. A slider's value readout (`fmt`) is a readout, not a label, and is left alone.
   - **Offsets, positions, limits (MUST).** 'X offset' / 'Y offset', the object first when one is needed ('Label X offset (px)'); 'X position' / 'Y position'; 'Maximum ...' in full, never 'Max ...'.
   - **Opacity (MUST).** A row that sets alpha says 'opacity' (*Faded opacity*, *Ready opacity*); no label says 'alpha'. The canonical row is *Master opacity* (§15).
   - **Rows a Master row multiplies (SHOULD).** They name their object (*Window scale*, *Panel scale*, *Container opacity*), and the tooltip ends with exactly 'Multiplied by Master scale on <location>.' or 'Multiplied by Master opacity on <location>.', where <location> is the *Master controls* tab's location string written per the next bullet: 'General > Master controls', or 'the General page > Master controls' in an addon that also has a General tab or rail entry.
   - **Location strings (MUST).** '<Page> > <Tab>[ > <Subsection>]' with ASCII ' > ' (never '->' or a triangle glyph); 'the General page > ...' wherever the addon also has a General tab or rail entry; every control quoted by its exact on-screen label. A rename greps `core/`, `modules/`, `locales/` and `settings/`, because tab names also live in drag-handle tooltips and chat route lines.
   - **Dependent rows (SHOULD).** A row that does nothing unless another is on says so in its own tooltip: 'Needs <exact row label>.', plus ' (<Page> > <Tab>)' when the parent is on another tab or page. Wording only: adding or removing `disabledIf` is not a label change.
   - **Acts on an instance (MUST).** *New <noun>*, *Duplicate <noun>*, *Delete <noun>*, *Reset <noun>*, no article. A checkbox on the selected instance reads *Enable this <noun>*, and *Lock this <noun>* (or *Unlock this <noun>* where the stored sense is unlocked), with <noun> the band picker's own noun (§14). *Delete ...* is the last act on its line.
   - **A button that opens a confirmation ends in '…' (MUST)** (U+2026). The one exception is the canonical *Reset all settings* (§12, §15): its name is quoted verbatim by §12, §20 and the library's Keybindings intro sentence, and it keeps it (recorded v2.88.0).
   - **Test and Preview (MUST).** A one-shot test button is *Test <thing>* (*Test notification*), never a bare *Test*, so it is not mistaken for §15's *Test mode*. *Preview* is reserved for a drawn preview. A tab that lists text is named for what it lists.
   - **Copy-from (MUST).** The section is *Copy settings from*; its labels and tooltip say exactly what is copied and what is not.
   - **No '+' (MUST)** as a word in a label or tooltip; write 'and'.
   - **Shared family names (SHOULD).** A simulator's pacing row is *Simulation step delay (seconds)* under a heading or tab named exactly *Simulator*, its tooltip opening 'Paces /<slash> sim: '; the slash verb goes in the tooltip, never in a heading. A data-lifetime tab is *History*: *Keep history for* (or a count such as *Runs to keep*), then the storage readout, then **Purge history…** last, with no builder-drawn heading over it (§7); an account-wide row's tooltip opens 'Account-wide: shared by every profile.' and its label carries no suffix. Per-instance visibility and fade sit under a *Visibility* subsection on the instance's General tab, their values match *General visibility*'s (*Always* / *Only in combat* / *Only out of combat* / *Never*), the hover toggle is *Fade unless hovered* and its slider *Faded opacity*.
   - **Commencement.** Each addon's next release after v2.88.0. A stray is a finding against this section (no anti-pattern; AUDIT.md's settings check (l), added by ruling (15)). A label change is never a migration: no stored path moves.
2. standards/standards/naming-cheatsheet.md: after the `Locale keys` row add `| Settings labels | Sentence case; '(px)', '(seconds)'; 'opacity', never 'alpha'; ASCII ' > ' in location strings (options-ui-§21) | *Window scale*, *Faded opacity*, *General > Master controls* |`.
3. The v2.88.0 entry intro (STANDARDS.md line 101): the bold title becomes `**Key bindings in a category of their own, a Keybindings tab in every windowed addon's settings, one frame-layering model, and one settings-layout vocabulary.**`; '(..., items 015 and 030)' becomes '(..., items 015, 020 and 030)'; replace the closing sentence that starts 'The run's other pending owner call on a ruled surface, CALL-02' and ends 'is not in this release.' with: 'Rulings (8) to (16) are the settings-layout item (020), ruled after the owner reviewed the per-addon layout preview: every proposed, unsuperseded change at confidence 50 or more lands, and the owner accepted the six calls put to them, among them CALL-02 (*Master alpha* is renamed *Master opacity*, a label and not a path) and CALL-05 (the swatch `disabledIf` question, U-13, is deferred to an issue).'
4. Changelog ruling `  **(8) options-ui-§21 (new): one settings vocabulary.**` The finding: the fifteen per-addon layout analyses each invented local wording rules because none was written down (LAYOUT_CROSS_ADDON U-11; XC-06, XC-08 to XC-13, XC-16, XC-17, XC-24, XC-25, XC-27, XC-29, XC-30), and no rule fixed capitalization. The ruling: one sentence per bullet; the multiplier sentence takes its location from the location-strings bullet, so it is never the bare form in an addon that has another General. The ripple: the naming-cheatsheet row; AUDIT.md check (l) and the context pack (15).

items.spec:
Same repo, branch and rules as WS-30 (no version bump; anchor on quoted text; changelog ruling shape and fixed numbering as WS-30 states). Design: LAYOUT_CROSS_ADDON U-05 (75%), XC-22 (60%), C12.

1. standards/standards/options-ui.md §7 (line 164). The paragraph beginning '**A tab that mixes control types MUST break them up with subsection headings, and those are NOT suppressed.**' (line 172): its opening becomes '**A tab that covers more than one subject MUST break it up with subsection headings, and those are NOT suppressed.** A subject is what the player is setting up (a bar, its background, its border), not a kind of widget: a tab holding a checkbox and a slider about one thing needs no heading.' Keep the rest, except 'A `subgroup` **MUST NOT** repeat its tab's name' becomes 'A `subgroup` **MUST NOT** restate its tab's name, stems included (a *Pricing* subsection under an *AH price* tab restates it)' (U-05d).
2. Directly after that paragraph and before '**One heading widget in the collection.**' add three paragraphs:
   - '**A leading master switch MAY sit unheaded.** One row that turns everything below it on or off MAY lead the tab above its first subsection heading, with no heading of its own. It is the only row that may (U-05b).'
   - '**A one-row subsection SHOULD merge** into a neighbor, unless its heading says something the row's label does not (a *Session* heading over a session-only row) (U-05c).'
   - '**No heading over an act; editors head their subjects too.** A heading is declared by a row, so a builder-drawn heading over a non-row act (a *Danger zone* over a purge button) is not allowed: the act goes last on its tab instead (options-ui-§21, *Shared family names*). A bespoke editor that draws no schema rows draws one `Heading` per subject through the library's `Section`, under every rule above (U-05e).'
3. §13's bullet '- **A tab that mixes control types MUST carry subsection headings** — see options-ui-§7.' (line 338) becomes '- **A tab that covers more than one subject MUST carry subsection headings** — see options-ui-§7. The tab label names the section; a heading inside it names each subject the section covers.' (U-05a).
4. Changelog ruling `  **(9) options-ui-§7: subjects, the lead switch and headings over acts.**` The finding: four addons read 'control types' as widget types, two resolved the lead-switch case in opposite directions (LAYOUT_CROSS_ADDON C12), and one drew a heading over a purge act (U-05, XC-22). The ruling: the four paragraphs. The ripple: §13's mirror bullet; AUDIT.md (l) (15).

standards/standards/options-ui.md §13 (line 322):
1. After the host-tab bullet ('- **A host tab** is drawn through `opts.tabs` ...', line 334) add:
   - '- **A tab holds at least two lines (SHOULD).** A section of one line is a subsection of a related tab, except a page's first tab, the Keybindings tab (§20), the only tab of a one-tab page and a host editor (a list, grid or tree) (U-06a).'
   - '- **Tab labels** are sentence case and join two subjects with "and" (options-ui-§21); sidebar page names are Title Case (U-06c).'
   - '- **Tab names under a rail.** A rail entry's tabs are named for what they hold, not after the entry. The first tab of a feature page or rail entry, holding the entry's switch, identity and acts, is *General*, also under a rail entry itself named *General* (the breadcrumb *General › General* is accepted). A tab that is not first and does not hold the basics gets a real name (U-07, XC-31).'

The bullet '- **The strip wraps.**': replace 'A page **SHOULD** hold its section count low enough for one row at default UI scale;' with 'A page **SHOULD** hold its section count low enough for one row at default UI scale: at most **eight** tab labels, and at most **six** on a page with a nav rail, whose strip is about 120 px narrower; past that, merge tabs (above) or adopt the rail (U-06b);' and keep the rest of the bullet.

The last bullet '- **The per-page Defaults button stays page-wide.**': append 'Its tooltip says what it resets, and is rewritten in the same change as any row move that changes that set; a row drawn on another page but reset here is named in it (§14). On a page with a nav rail it reads, exactly, "Restore every tab of the entry selected on the left, for the <instance> in the band, to its defaults.", with <instance> the band picker's noun (XC-28).'

Changelog ruling `  **(10) options-ui-§13: thin tabs, the strip budget, tab names and Defaults tooltips.**` The finding: every per-addon file merged lonely tabs, four asked for a strip number, two names for a rail entry's first tab collided (C17), and five Defaults tooltips were stale or under-stated (U-06, U-07, XC-22, XC-28, XC-31). items.title: options-ui-§14: the band's height never depends on the selection, a row is stamped to the page that draws it unless both Defaults tooltips say otherwise, one link vocabulary, a stored per-instance lock is an act, PageBanner acts recorded not ruled (U-08a-e, XC-14, XC-15)
items.spec:
Same repo, branch and rules as WS-30. Design: LAYOUT_CROSS_ADDON U-08 (65%), XC-14 (60%), XC-15 (65%), XC-16. U-08(d), a `PageBanner{ acts = ... }` arm, is NOT ruled: this run adds no such library surface (one accepted consumer, which draws an `O.PageHeader` block as its own analysis specifies); it is recorded in open-evolutions by WS-37.

standards/standards/options-ui.md §14 (line 347):
1. After the bullet '- **The rail is not a picker.**' (line 356) add '- **The band's height MUST NOT depend on the selected instance.** Every instance draws the same cells, so the strip and the page below do not move when the picker changes; a cell that does not apply to the selected instance stays empty rather than collapsing (U-08a).'
2. After the paragraph that starts '**Controls that apply to every tab MUST sit in that band too**' add the paragraph '**A row is stamped to the page that draws it (SHOULD); one that is not says so (MUST).** A row drawn in a page's band or on its tabs SHOULD carry that page's `page` (or `panel`) key, so that page's Defaults resets it. A row MAY stay stamped to another page, to keep the set a Defaults button resets unchanged when the row is drawn elsewhere, but then both pages' Defaults tooltips **MUST** say so: the drawing page's says the row is not reset there, and the owning page's names it among what it resets (§13). A row drawn on one page and reset, silently, by another page's Defaults is the failure this rule exists for. Moving or re-stamping a row is no migration (a page key is not a stored path), and the tooltips are rewritten in the same change (U-08b, XC-14).'
3. After the paragraph that starts '**The band is ONE ROW**' and its three conditions, and before 'A page taking this escape has **one** band row', add:
   - '- **Linked instances use one vocabulary (SHOULD).** A *Link to <Source>* checkbox, a *Copy from <Source>* button and, on the linked instance's tabs, the hint "Linked to <Source>. Untick Link to <Source> above to give this unit its own look.", with *unit* the band picker's noun (U-08c, XC-15).'
   - '- **A stored per-instance lock is one of the instance's acts.** It goes in the band or on the `General` escape with the other acts, labeled per options-ui-§21 (*Lock this <noun>*), never on a size or position tab (U-08e).'
   - '- **Acts beside the picker on one row (recorded).** `O.PageBanner` draws the picker and at most one `action`. A band holding the picker and further acts on one row is one `O.PageHeader` block with the picker inside it (this section's at-most-one-block rule). A banner arm taking several acts is an open evolution, not ruled at v2.88.0.'
4. Changelog ruling `  **(11) options-ui-§14: a fixed band, rows stamped to their page or disclosed, the link words, the instance lock.**` The finding: four addons hit the one-row band; one left moved rows stamped to the page they left, so that page's Defaults reset rows no longer on it with neither tooltip saying so (C3), while two accepted changes keep band rows stamped to another page on purpose so no Defaults scope changes; one concept had five names in one addon and three in another (C4) (U-08, XC-14, XC-15). The ruling: re-stamping is the default; a cross-page stamp is legal only when both Defaults tooltips disclose it. The ripple: §13's Defaults bullet; AUDIT.md (l); open-evolutions (15).

items.title: options-ui-§15: Master opacity (CALL-02), composed words extended only through notes / resetPositionTooltip / lockIsPreview, the frameless packing (Minimap beside Debug console when Lock frame is omitted; Minimap and Test mode bullets amended), the omitted-row hole intended, Lock frame singular, the extras test and the Behavior tab, Reset all settings keeps its name (U-01, U-09a-f, XC-04, XC-05, XC-23); anti-pattern #106; Master alpha swept from the live docs
items.spec:
Same repo, branch and rules as WS-30. Design: LAYOUT_CROSS_ADDON U-01 (80%), U-09 (55%), XC-04 (75%), XC-05 (65%), XC-23 (60%), CALL-02. THE LIBKA0S SURFACE this rule names (LK-30 MUST match exactly), `LibKa0s-Options-1.0` OptionsCompose, from `LibKa0s v1.77.0`: `MasterControls` spec fields `notes = { <leaf> = string }` (leaves `enabled`, `visibility`, `scale`, `alpha`, `locked`, `debugConsole`, `minimap`, `testMode`, and the buttons `resetPosition`, `resetAll`; one sentence appended after the canonical tooltip with one space), `resetPositionTooltip = string` (replaces the *Reset position* tooltip; a `notes.resetPosition` still appends after it), `lockIsPreview = true` (the *Lock frame* tooltip becomes exactly: Stop the frame being dragged. While it is unlocked the display shows placeholder content, so it can be seen and placed; this is the addon's test mode.); the alpha row's label *Master opacity*; with `locked` omitted (frameless, or `omit.locked`) and *Debug console* present, *Minimap button* pairs beside *Debug console*, and *Test mode*, where the addon has one, opens its own line.

standards/standards/options-ui.md §15 (line 374):
1. Table line 383 `| Master scale | Master alpha |` -> `| Master scale | Master opacity |`. Under the table add: '*Master opacity* was *Master alpha* until v2.88.0 (owner call CALL-02). Only the label changed: the stored leaf is still `alpha`, so nothing migrates.'
2. Bullet '- **An addon with no movable frame omits exactly the frame-only rows** — master scale, master alpha, lock frame, reset position': 'master alpha' -> 'master opacity'; 'the per-instance scale/alpha/lock' -> 'the per-instance scale/opacity/lock'. Append: '**The frameless packing.** With *Lock frame* omitted, *Minimap button* leaves the first column and sits beside *Debug console*, so no line holds a lone control. A frameless tab (which has no *Test mode*, see the Test mode bullet) therefore reads [Enable <AddonName>][General visibility] / [Debug console][Minimap button], then *Reset all settings* alone. A framed addon that omits only *Lock frame* reads ... / [Debug console][Minimap button] / [Test mode], *Test mode* opening its own line. The library's composer lays both out so from `LibKa0s v1.77.0` (U-09c). **Any other omitted row leaves its cell empty, and that is intended**: the canonical rows never reflow, so each row is always in the same cell (U-09d).'
3. Bullet '- **Minimap button belongs here, in every addon, and it takes the FIRST column of its line.**': after that bold lead add '(The frameless packing above is the one exception: where *Lock frame* is omitted it takes the second column, beside *Debug console*.)'
4. Bullet '- **Test mode belongs here, in every addon with a positionable display.**': after 'beside *Minimap button* (whose first-column position the bullet above explains)' insert ', or, where *Lock frame* is omitted and *Minimap button* has moved beside *Debug console*, on its own line below them (the frameless-packing exception)'.
5. After the bullet '- **The rows are composed, not hand-written**' add:
   - '- **The composed rows' words are the composer's (MUST).** A host **MUST NOT** write the label or tooltip text of a row or button `MasterControls` emits, whether by patching the returned rows, by passing `labels`, or by keeping a copy. Where the canonical tooltip misdescribes the addon it passes, from `LibKa0s v1.77.0`: `notes = { <leaf> = "One sentence." }`, which appends one sentence after the canonical tooltip (leaves `enabled`, `visibility`, `scale`, `alpha`, `locked`, `debugConsole`, `minimap`, `testMode`, and the buttons `resetPosition` and `resetAll`); `resetPositionTooltip`, which replaces the *Reset position* tooltip, the one canonical text that has to name the addon's own frames; and `lockIsPreview = true`, below. A host override shipped before v2.88.0 moves onto these at the addon's next release on `LibKa0s v1.77.0` (U-01, XC-04). Any other rewrite is **anti-pattern #106**.'
   - '- **Lock frame stays singular (recorded).** In an addon with several movable frames it is still the addon-wide lock and keeps its name; `notes.locked` says which frames it covers (U-09b).'
   - '- **The unlocked view as the test mode.** An addon whose unlocked view is its test mode (the exemption the Test mode bullet states) passes `lockIsPreview = true`, and *Lock frame* takes the library's one tooltip for it, quoted exactly as above. What the addon does at combat start is said, where it is true, in `notes.locked` (U-01, XC-05).'
6. The extras bullet's terms: 'as the per-instance scale, alpha and lock do' -> 'as the per-instance scale, opacity and lock do'; add a term '  - It **MUST** be a player-facing switch the player looks for beside *Enable*, and there are at most two. A performance knob (an update throttle, a refresh interval, a merge-pets switch) is not one: it goes on a General-page tab named **Behavior**. A simulator or developer knob is never an extra (U-09e, XC-23).'
7. Bullet '- **The two resets are the tab's closing button pair**': append '*Reset all settings* keeps its name with no ellipsis although it opens a confirmation, options-ui-§21's one exception (U-09f).'
8. standards/standards/anti-patterns.md: append `106. **A composed row's words rewritten by the host** — the label or tooltip of a row or button `MasterControls` emits changed by patching the returned rows, by `labels` or by a copy, instead of through `notes`, `resetPositionTooltip` or `lockIsPreview` (options-ui-§15).` STANDARDS.md line 81 `(#1–#105)` -> `(#1–#106)`.
9. COPY_GROUPS is keyed by stored config groups (frame, header, rows, bars, text, icons, tooltip, visibility, columns, data), not by settings page. So a page move changes no Copy group unless a stored path moves, and stored paths never move in this run.
